issues.claim: §4.11 *The clock* (1) (base l. 8453–8454) defines the document's current week as "the week of the last folded event that carries one" (also §2.9's `EpochRecord` comment, l. 3140, and J-A67.45's index row, l. 22742). R5-03's (4) (l. 8475–8487) and V08 §3.6 (6) (l. 1944–1947) fold a late change "after the last epoch at `W₀` + 1 where `W₁` is after `W₀`, else at `W₀`" and claim that therefore "the document's current week never falls back". That holds only against `W₀`. Between epochs, an absorb with no year end, crossing or calamity folds its element events standalone at their weeks after `W₀` (V08 §3.6 (3), (6)), the usual weekly sync. So after an absorb that folds a Works-beginning change at `W₀` + 3, the next absorb's late change is appended at `W₀` + 1, and by (1) the current week falls back to `W₀` + 1. The drawn present (J-A67.45; *Works* (9)) and every export then show that Works before its start: the house staked a sync ago vanishes. A clock turned back, or a change dated in (`W₀`, current week), does the same. Two builders differ: one derives (1) literally, the other keeps "never falls back". T-V8-49 (g)'s bar ("current week after the absorb not before `W₀`", V08 l. 3311) and T76-1's ("never before it", base l. 18245–18247) pass the regression.
issues.required_change: 1. §4.11 *The clock* (1): "The document's current week is derived — the week of the last folded event that carries one — never a stored counter (§2.9)" → "The document's current week is derived — the greatest week the folded events carry, so an event folded after one of a later week (a late change at `W₀` + 1 or `W₀`, (4); a dossier change dated before an event an earlier absorb folded) never moves it back — never a stored counter (§2.9)". 2. Ends: (model) §2.9's `EpochRecord` comment "the week of the last folded event that carries one" → "the greatest week the folded events carry"; (scope) J-A67.45's index row "(the last folded event's)" → "(the greatest folded week, §4.11 *The clock* (1))"; (V08) T-V8-49 (g), after "the document's current week after the absorb not before `W₀`", adds "; and on a copy, an absorb past `W₀` with no year end, crossing or calamity folding a standalone change at `W₀` + 3 that begins a Works, then an absorb carrying a non-calamity change dated at or before `W₀` — folded at `W₀` + 1, the document's current week still `W₀` + 3 and that Works drawn at its stage there"; (scope) T76-1's late non-calamity clause "the document's current week never before it" → "the document's current week never before it nor before the week of any event an earlier absorb folded". (The adjudicator may instead keep (1) and fold every newly carried change dated before the current week at that week, its tick in its receipt; the bars above then read the same.)

issues.claim: R5-03 holds a late calamity carried by an absorb whose week is not after `W₀` "for the first epoch a later absorb folds" (base §4.11 *The clock* (4) l. 8483; V08 §3.6 (3) l. 1871–1876; §7.7's comment l. 11825). V08 §3.6 (4) (l. 1903–1908) writes the whole held list in every `dossierFacts` event ("the binding's list less each calamity the first epoch this absorb folds carries, plus each late calamity this absorb holds"). So a later absorb past `W₀` that folds no epoch must write the list unchanged and fold no epoch for the held calamity, unlike a newly carried late one with `W₁` after `W₀`, for which "the port folds one at `W₁`". The calamity waits up to the next year end. That is the common path: weekly syncs between year ends fold none. T-V8-49 (g) (V08 l. 3311) and T76-1 (base l. 18242–18245) hold the calamity and then make the very next absorb fold an epoch (a population move past the tolerance). So two wrong builds pass every bar, T-V8-5's fold check included. One writes `lateCalamities` from this absorb's new holds alone, so the list empties at a no-epoch absorb and the calamity is silently lost. The other folds an epoch at `W₁` for a held calamity. VV78-r5-01 names this wait but tests only a forked copy.
issues.required_change: T-V8-49 (g), after "the next absorb past `W₀` folding the crossing and the calamity's strike at its first epoch's first week, its deaths in that epoch's burial need", add: "; and on a copy, between the hold and that absorb, an absorb past `W₀` with no year end, no crossing and no calamity (one institution's `state` changed) — no epoch folded, its `dossierFacts` event listing the held calamity in `lateCalamities`, the calamity not struck — then an absorb past the next year end folding the year-end epoch, the calamity riding it at its first week `W₀` + 1, struck once, its deaths in that epoch's burial need, `lateCalamities` empty after".

issues.claim: R5-03 adds `DossierBinding.lateCalamities: string[]`, "the binding keys of late calamities held" (§7.7 l. 11825). A held calamity's `CalamityRef` is built "from its carried `calamity` fact under the held key" (V08 §3.6 (3) l. 1894–1895). The calamity key is a port-minted binding key (`calamity:<week>:<slug(name)>`, V08 §2.3). At a line change, "B's `fromLines` entry for A re-keys the binding rows (a `rebind` `setAttr` per changed key …)", and an entry may be a `table` of `{ from, to }` rows (V08 §2.4 l. 587; §3.8 l. 2042–2047; §2.3's row life l. 566). Nothing re-keys `lateCalamities`, nor `quarantined[].key`, which has the same gap. Where the migrating or a later absorb folds the epoch the held calamity rides, a builder who re-keys rows and carried facts alone looks up the old key and finds no fact. The result is a crash, or the calamity silently lost against R5-03's "never lost". A quarantined record's stale key likewise stops shielding it from the diff. Two builders differ, and the case is not in the canon's catalogue (no migration entry for V08 §3.8's binding lists). T-V8-11 (l. 3273) runs only `identity` and the missing-entry hold.
issues.required_change: 1. V08 §3.8's line-change bullet, after "re-keys the binding rows (a `rebind` `setAttr` per changed key, V08 §3.6 (5), no address changes)", add: ", and every binding key the binding's lists hold — each `quarantined` entry's `key` and each `lateCalamities` key — by the same entry in that absorb, before the diff, the absorb's `dossierFacts` event carrying both lists under the new keys (V08 §3.6 (4)); a key the entry does not map keeps its key". 2. V08 §2.6's `DossierBinding.lateCalamities` row, its migrate cell, adds "; a line migration re-keys it by the `fromLines` entry (V08 §3.8)". 3. T-V8-11 adds: "on its test line with a `fromLines` table that re-keys calamity keys, a document holding a late calamity (T-V8-49 (g)'s second absorb) and a quarantined record, migrated by an absorb that folds an epoch — the calamity riding that epoch under its new key, struck once, `lateCalamities` empty after, and the quarantined record's key re-keyed, its carried state still skipped by the diff".

issues.claim: Before round 5, §2.7's support step (6) ended (`3310b53` l. 2615): "so a locked or pinned raised way is crossed as an unlocked one is (§7.4's lock column; T110-2)". R5-02's rewrite leaves only "A lock or pin holds the same" (base l. 2587), and §7.4's lock column says "its deck and piers held, as every raised way is from its creation" (l. 11403). Meanwhile §7.1's general row (l. 10587) refuses `refuse.locked` a map event that "crosses … a locked or pinned entity — a drawn way across a locked entity", and §7.2's test (l. 10815) refuses "a drawn way across a locked footprint". The `bend.raised.underSpan`/`bend.raised.around` row (l. 10632) and the `bend.wall.raisedCrossing` row (l. 10631) say only "a standing raised way". So a ground `drawWay`, a moved way or a hand carve across a locked raised way matches both a refusal and a bend. T110-2 (4) (l. 18491–18500) runs the hand `drawWall` with the raised way locked and expects the bend, which settles walls. Neither T110-2 (5)'s hand roads (l. 18500–18503) nor T-V9-52 (V09 l. 4404) runs a lock. So one builder refuses the road and another bends it under a span or round the raised way, and both pass every bar.
issues.required_change: 1. §7.1's lock row, cause: "— a drawn way across a locked entity," → "— a drawn way across a locked entity (but not a ground way, a carve or a wall stretch passing beneath a locked or pinned raised way's deck, which changes none of its parts and is bent by the `bend.raised.underSpan`, `bend.raised.around` and `bend.wall.raisedCrossing` rows as beneath an unlocked one: §2.7's support step (6), a lock or pin holds the same),". 2. `bend.raised.underSpan`'s row, cause: "meeting a standing raised way's supports" → "meeting a standing raised way's — locked, pinned or neither — supports"; `bend.wall.raisedCrossing`'s row: "across a standing raised way" → "across a standing raised way, locked, pinned or neither". 3. END (scope): T110-2 (5), after "a hand road wider than every `open` span's clear width drawn across one", add ", each hand road run again with the raised way locked and with it pinned — the same outcome, no `refuse.locked`".
